claims.text: Put \(q=n-r\). For nonempty rectangular data \(i,j\ge1\), \(N>1\) holds exactly when \[ 1\le i\le q-1,\qquad 1\le j\le r-1. \] Indeed, \(b\ge1\), while \(a\ge1\) exactly under these two strict inequalities; then \(\binom{a+b}{a}\ge2\). If \(i=q\) or \(j=r\), then \(a=0\) and \(N=1\).

Interpreting “immediately beyond” as enlarging the tested rectangle to \(r\le5,\ q\le6\), the admissible new parameter instances with \(N>1\) are: \[ \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} r&q=n-r& (i,j)&\#\\ \hline 5&2,3,4,5,6& 1\le i\le q-1,\ 1\le j\le4&4(q-1)\\ 2,3,4&6& 1\le i\le5,\ 1\le j\le r-1&5(r-1) \end{array} \] Equivalently, these are \((r,n)=(5,7),(5,8),(5,9),(5,10),(5,11)\) and \((2,8),(3,9),(4,10)\), with the indicated \((i,j)\). The overlap \((r,q)=(5,6)\) occurs only in the first row. There are \(60+30=90\) such \((r,q,i,j)\)-instances.
The two Schur generating families are minimal for each of these 90 instances; this is not established by their enumeration.
